resolutions.finding: C1: R027 files 'does anything else call Tour.present' as unresolved while R023 already documents SettingsView.swift:970; both miss AppCommands.swift:101-103.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Repo-wide grep for `Tour.present` returns exactly 3 shipped call sites plus 1 capture-only controller call, counted by listing them:
  (1) DroppyCode/App/AppCommands.swift:101-103 - `CommandGroup(replacing: .help) { Button("Welcome tour") { Tour.present(model: model) } }`. Exact literal menu title: "Welcome tour".
  (2) DroppyCode/App/AppDelegate.swift:18-19 - `if !windows.model.settings.hasSeenTour { Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(700)); Tour.present(model: windows.model) } }`. The 700 ms literal is real: the tour appears 700 ms after applicationDidFinishLaunching, after showMain() and openThreadOnLaunch().
  (3) DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:970 - `Button("Show") { Tour.present(model: model) }.buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small)` inside the About app card's "Welcome tour" ChromeRow.
  (4) Capture-only, NOT Tour.present: DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift:216 calls `TourWindowController.shared.present(pages: Tour.pages)` directly (see G5).
Tour.present itself (TourPages.swift:26-28) is exactly: `TourWindowController.shared.present(pages: pages, onFinish: { model.settings.hasSeenTour = true }, onClose: { model.settings.hasSeenTour = true })` - both closures write the same flag.
ENGINEERING DECISION on the critic's wording: `CommandGroup(replacing: .help)` replaces the standard help command group's items (the one 'Droppy Code Help' item), not the whole Help menu; AppKit still supplies the Help menu title and its search field. Saying it 'REPLACES the entire standard Help menu' overstates it.
Persistence: AppSettings.swift:177 Key `hasSeenTour` = "hasSeenTour"; property at :532-534 writes on didSet; loaded at :745 as `defaults.object(forKey:) as? Bool ?? false`.
resolutions.port_impact: The port needs a Help-menu item labelled exactly "Welcome tour" that replays the tour, a Settings > About row button labelled "Show", and a first-run trigger gated on the persisted `hasSeenTour` boolean (default false) with a 700 ms delay after the main window is shown. Both finishing and closing the tour must set hasSeenTour = true.

resolutions.finding: C2: R023 puts the About app card first and lists AboutSoftwareUpdateSection / AboutUpdateCheckRow / AboutUpdateChromeAccessory only in calls_into; neither report gives the About page's row order.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. AboutSettingsPage.body (SettingsView.swift:926-949) is a `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: Chrome.sectionSpacing)` whose children are, in order:
  1. `AboutSoftwareUpdateSection()` (line 928)
  2. `appCard` (line 929)
  3. `ChromeSection(title: "Credits")` (line 930) containing, in order: MadeByDroppyRow(url: https://getdroppy.app) / divider / ChromeRow "Working indicators" detail "Ported from Zeron by Wing, MIT License." with CreditLink "zeronsh/zeron" -> https://github.com/zeronsh/zeron / divider / ChromeRow "Terminal" detail "SwiftTerm by Miguel de Icaza, MIT License." with CreditLink "SwiftTerm" -> https://github.com/migueldeicaza/SwiftTerm / divider / ChromeRow "Welcome tour" detail "Ported from TourKit by Ram Patra, MIT License." with CreditLink "rampatra/TourKit" -> https://github.com/rampatra/TourKit / divider / LicensesRow(). That is 5 rows and 4 dividers.
appCard (SettingsView.swift:951-988) is one ChromeCard whose children are, in order: icon+name+version HStack (NSApp.applicationIconImage at 56x56, `Text("Droppy Code")` 15pt semibold, `Text(verbatim: "Version <AppInfo.version> (<AppInfo.build>)")` 12pt secondary, padding 16) / ChromeRowDivider / ChromeRow(title: "Welcome tour", detail: "The slideshow from the first launch: Hydra, the effort slider, panels and themes.") with Button("Show") / ChromeRowDivider / `AboutUpdateCheckRow()` (line 973) / ChromeRowDivider / body text "The coding app by Droppy: a native home for your coding agents, built in Swift with Liquid Glass." (13pt) / ChromeRowDivider / license line "Droppy Code is licensed under the GNU AGPL v3.0 with attribution terms; SwiftTerm is MIT licensed." (12pt secondary). Both text rows use `.padding(.leading, 16).padding(.trailing, Chrome.rowControlTrailingPadding).padding(.vertical, 11)`.
A THIRD placement the family missed entirely: `AboutUpdateChromeAccessory()` is NOT on the About page body at all - it is in the Settings chrome row, SettingsView.swift:255-257, inside `if page == .about`, alongside the sibling accessories `ChromeSearchField(prompt: "Search servers")` for .mcp, `ProvidersRefreshButton()` for .providers and `ArchiveDeleteAllButton()` for .archive.
SOURCE FACT with layout consequence: AboutSoftwareUpdateSection (AboutUpdateViews.swift:719-753) renders release cards only `if checker.updateAvailable, let update = checker.update`; with no update it is an empty VStack that still runs `.task { if progress.consumePendingCelebration() { startCelebrationSweep() }; await checker.check() }`. So on the common path it draws nothing but still triggers an update check every time About appears.
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows About page must place the software-update section above the app card, put the update-check row inside the app card between the "Welcome tour" row and the body text, and put the version pill / update accessory in the settings window's chrome strip (only while the About page is selected), not in the page body. Opening About must kick off an update check.

resolutions.finding: C3: R028's ui_elements describes the second ProviderIcon as unconditional while its feature note says the heads icon is drawn whenever headsProvider is non-nil, unlike UsagePanel.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. UsageFloatingPanel.swift:80-88 strip: `HStack(spacing: 6) { ProviderIcon(provider: provider, size: 12); if let headsProvider { ProviderIcon(provider: headsProvider, size: 12) }; Text("Usage").font(.system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium)).foregroundStyle(Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.92)) }`. The second icon IS conditional, but only on `headsProvider != nil` (line 82) - there is no `!= provider` test.
UsagePanel.swift:29 computes `let heads: ProviderKind? = (headsProvider != nil && headsProvider != provider) ? headsProvider : nil`, so the body suppresses a heads section when the pair's heads run on the lead's own provider.
Consequence (SOURCE FACT): when a Hydra pair's heads use the same provider as the lead, the floating panel's title capsule draws the same provider icon twice, while the body shows one merged section. The critic's feature-note reading is right; its ui_elements complaint is right that the two sections of R028 disagree, but the critic's own wording ("with no condition") restates R028's error rather than the source: the condition exists, it is simply the weaker one.
resolutions.port_impact: Port the strip literally: draw the heads icon whenever a heads provider is set, including when it equals the lead's, so the duplicate icon is reproduced. Do not 'fix' it to match the body's rule.

resolutions.finding: G1: DiffInspector.swift show() guard order is stated backwards by R018; the session counter is bumped before the isShown guard.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. DiffPopoverCoordinator.show() is DiffInspector.swift:627-636 (the critic cites 626-632; off by one):
  627 private func show() {
  628   guard let runtime, let target = resolvedAnchor() else { return }
  629   session += 1
  630   guard !popover.isShown else { return }
  631   popover.setFixedContent(DiffInspector(runtime: runtime), size: NSSize(width: Self.width, height: Self.height))
  632   startMonitors()
  633   shownOn = target.view
  634   shownRuntime = runtime
  635   popover.show(relativeTo: target.view.bounds, of: target.view, preferredEdge: target.edge)
So the order is: anchor guard, THEN session += 1, THEN the isShown guard. The critic has the order exactly right.
The critic's CAUSAL claim is WRONG in detail. Counters: `session` and `pendingSession` both start at 0 (lines 531-532). `pendingSession` is assigned in exactly two places: close() (576-577) and reopen()'s anchor-changed branch (607-608), each as `session += 1; pendingSession = session`, which RE-SYNCHRONIZES them. show() bumps `session` alone (629). Therefore after ANY show() the pair is unequal, and popoverDidClose's guard `if self.session == self.pendingSession` (line 649) is false - not just after an extra show() on an already-shown popover. Any close routed through close() restores equality before performClose, so the guard passes on every app-initiated dismissal.
The real exposure: a close the coordinator did not initiate (NSPopover.behavior = .semitransient, line 536, closing itself; or the anchor view leaving its window) reaches popoverDidClose with session != pendingSession, so it does NOT clear `shownRuntime.isDiffVisible` and does NOT set `popover.contentViewController = nil` (lines 650-654). That is reachable from the very first show(), with no extra show() calls at all.
setAnchor(_:) (542-545) and setFallbackAnchor(_:) (583-586) do call show() unconditionally under `if desiredVisible`, as the critic says; that path merely adds more unmatched bumps, it is not the cause.
resolutions.port_impact: Port the counter pair exactly, including that a show bumps only the open counter. Reproduce the consequence: a popover that closes itself leaves the thread's isDiffVisible flag set and the panel content alive. Do not add a resynchronizing write in the show path.

resolutions.finding: G2: MCPSettingsPage.swift:563-565 deletes a custom server with no confirmation and no consult of settings.confirmBeforeDeleting.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPSettingsPage.swift:564-566: `PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true) { model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) }` - no popover, no confirmationDialog, no settings read.
`confirmBeforeDeleting` appears at exactly 9 lines repo-wide, counted: AppSettings.swift:123 (Key `confirmDelete` = "confirmBeforeDeleting"), :209 and :210 (property + didSet), :702 (load, `as? Bool ?? true`, so the DEFAULT IS TRUE); SettingsView.swift:361 (the SettingsSwitch that toggles it), :851 (ArchiveDeleteAllButton), :892 (ArchiveSettingsPage per-row Delete); SidebarView.swift:192, :360, :891. MCPSettingsPage.swift contains the string zero times.
What the delete does: MCPStore.deleteCustom (MCPStore.swift:193-199) calls `disconnect(entry.catalogEntry())` - which itself cancels the probe, runs `MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry)` (MCPStore.swift:124), signs out of OAuth and unregisters the proxy for an OAuth entry, clears connections/states/drafts, save(), exportAll() - then removes the server from `customs` and calls saveCustoms(). So one unconfirmed click destroys the server definition AND its Keychain secrets.
Note the archive paths the critic cites are at SettingsView.swift:851 and :892 (not 838-870 / 903-919 as written), and they are not symmetric with each other: ArchiveDeleteAllButton uses a popover (PopoverMenu with PopoverSectionHeader/PopoverNote/PopoverItem), ArchiveSettingsPage uses a `.confirmationDialog`.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce: the MCP custom-server Delete is a single-click destructive action that ignores the confirm-before-deleting preference. Do not add a confirmation to the port. Carry the preference's exact key name "confirmBeforeDeleting" and default true for the paths that do read it.

resolutions.finding: G3: MCPKeyPanel.present has no isPresenting re-entry guard while MCPSetupPanel.present does; a second present re-opens the browser and rebuilds the view.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. MCPKeyPanel.present is MCPKeyPanel.swift:15-31 and starts straight in with side effects:
  16-18  `if let keysURL = entry.keysURL, let url = URL(string: keysURL) { NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) }`
  19-21  builds MCPKeyPanelView(...).presentedChrome().environment(model)
  22     `let height = NSHostingView(rootView: content.frame(width: 380)).fittingSize.height.rounded(.up)`
  23-25  `let panel = self.panel ?? makePanel(); panel.contentViewController = NSHostingController(rootView: content); panel.setContentSize(NSSize(width: 380, height: max(height, 100)))`
  26-28  `if let visible = NSScreen.main?.visibleFrame { panel.setFrameOrigin(NSPoint(x: visible.maxX - 380 - 24, y: visible.maxY - panel.frame.height - 24)) }`
  29-30  startEscapeMonitor(); panel.orderFrontRegardless()
There is no `presentedEntryID` field and close() (33-36) is only `stopEscapeMonitor(); panel?.orderOut(nil)`.
MCPSetupPanel.swift has `private var presentedEntryID: String?` (line 12), `func isPresenting(_ entry:) -> Bool { panel?.isVisible == true && presentedEntryID == entry.id }` (18-20), the early return `if isPresenting(entry) { panel?.orderFrontRegardless(); return }` (23-26), sets presentedEntryID at 27, and clears it in close() at 47. Its width is 400 (34, 37, 39) against the key panel's 380; both floor the height at 100.
Reachable repeat call sites for MCPKeyPanel.shared.present, counted from grep: MCPSettingsPage.swift:356 (MCPServerCard.begin()), :538 (MCPCustomRow.begin()), :973 (MCPInfoPopover's `Button("Change the <label>...")`). MCPSetupPanel.shared.present has 2 call sites: :288 and :342, plus the runtime re-fit at MCPSetupPanel.swift:184.
resolutions.port_impact: Port both panels as separate singletons with the asymmetry intact: the setup panel is idempotent for the same entry (refocus only), the key panel re-opens the external keys URL and rebuilds its content on every present. Reproduce the 380 vs 400 widths and the 100px minimum height.

resolutions.finding: G4: R027 files Tour.present's other call sites as unresolvable from TourPages.swift alone.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT - same evidence as C1. Three shipped call sites (AppCommands.swift:102, AppDelegate.swift:19, SettingsView.swift:970) and one capture-only controller call (TourCaptures.swift:216). R027's omission of the `.milliseconds(700)` literal in the AppDelegate note is a real gap; the literal is `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(700))` on AppDelegate.swift:19, inside `Task { @MainActor in ... }`, guarded by `if !windows.model.settings.hasSeenTour` on line 18.
Also on that path: AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching returns EARLY when `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` (AppDelegate.swift:11-14, `Task { await WebsiteCaptures.run(model: windows.model) }; return`), so in a capture run the first-run tour gate is never evaluated at all.
resolutions.port_impact: The port's first-run tour must be suppressed in any equivalent capture/automation mode, and the Help-menu and About-page replays must be available regardless of hasSeenTour.

resolutions.finding: G5: TourCaptures.swift:216-220 drives TourWindowController with no onFinish and no onClose; nobody classified this capture-only path.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. TourCaptures.swift:213-221:
  WebsiteCaptures.log("scene tour-window"); stage.setBackdrop(backdropView(.welcome)); stage.setWindowHidden(true)
  216 `let tourWindow = TourWindowController.shared.present(pages: Tour.pages)`
  217 `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)`
  218 `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(1_400))`
  219 `await recorder.still("tour-window", Stage.tourRect(around: tourWindow.frame))`
  220 `TourWindowController.shared.close()`
  221 `stage.setWindowHidden(false)`
TourWindowController.present's signature defaults are `width: CGFloat = 660, continueButtonTitle: String = "Continue", finishButtonTitle: String = "Done", onFinish: (() -> Void)? = nil, onClose: (() -> Void)? = nil`, so the capture call gets width 660 and both nil closures; inside TourView's onFinish wrapper, `if let onFinish { onFinish() } else { onClose?() }` - with both nil, nothing is written, so hasSeenTour is never set in a capture run. `@discardableResult` on present (line 18) is what lets the other call sites ignore the returned NSWindow.
Reachability: this is shipped, non-debug code reached only when the binary is launched with `--tour-captures <folder>` (CaptureRun.swift:9-19 scans CommandLine.arguments for `--website-captures` and `--tour-captures`; isTourRun at :21-25; WebsiteCaptures.swift:304 `if isTourRun { await TourCaptures.run(model: model); return }`). No #if DEBUG guards it; the documented invocation is in TourCaptures.swift:7: `open -n -W "Droppy Code.app" --args --tour-captures <folder>`.
resolutions.port_impact: The port does not need the capture harness. If it keeps one, the controller API must allow presenting with no completion callbacks, and the tour-seen flag must be written by the callbacks, not by the controller.

resolutions.finding: G6: UsageFloatingPanel.hasSomething (fraction only) vs UsagePanel.showsContext (fraction AND windowTokens) can render an empty 16pt-padded VStack instead of the placeholder.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT that disproves it: `ContextUsage` (Core/Models/Timeline.swift:297-305) has stored `usedTokens: Int` and `windowTokens: Int?`, and `fraction` is a COMPUTED property:
  301 `var fraction: Double? {`
  302 `    guard let windowTokens, windowTokens > 0 else { return nil }`
  303 `    return min(1, Double(usedTokens) / Double(windowTokens))`
So `fraction != nil` IMPLIES `windowTokens != nil` (and > 0). A ContextUsage 'carrying a fraction but no windowTokens' cannot exist. UsagePanel.swift:32's `showsContext = usage?.fraction != nil && usage?.windowTokens != nil` is redundant, not stricter, and the `if let usage, let fraction = usage.fraction, let window = usage.windowTokens` at :34 always succeeds when fraction is non-nil.
Exhaustive check of the empty-render claim over UsageFloatingPanel.swift:27-29's four disjuncts: (a) fraction != nil -> showsContext true -> the context row and UsageBar render; (b) PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits(provider) -> showsLimits true -> PlanLimitsView renders in the no-heads branch, or providerSection(provider, role:"Lead") renders in the heads branch; (c) CreditsReader.exposesCredits(provider) -> symmetric; (d) headsProvider exposes limits or credits -> if headsProvider != provider, providerSection(heads, role:"Heads") renders; if headsProvider == provider then (b) or (c) already holds. There is no combination where hasSomething is true and UsagePanel's VStack is empty.
Supporting literals: PlanLimits.swift:68-70 `exposesLimits` is true for exactly 7 providers, counted: .codex, .claude, .antigravity, .copilot, .commandcode, .zai, .pi. ProviderCredits.swift:58 `exposesCredits` is true for exactly 2: .deepseek, .commandcode. Both are pure functions of ProviderKind with no runtime state, so they cannot flip between the two predicates' evaluations.
resolutions.port_impact: No port action beyond copying both predicates as written. Do NOT 'reconcile' them; the redundant windowTokens test is harmless. The port's context-usage model must keep fraction derived from windowTokens so the implication holds.

resolutions.finding: G7: R022 leaves AppSettings.modelListLimit unresolved.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. `static let modelListLimit = 15` at DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:181. Exactly 4 references repo-wide, counted:
  AppSettings.swift:181 (definition)
  AppSettings.swift:819 - `guard !modelList.contains(pin), modelList.count < Self.modelListLimit else { return }` inside `addToModelList(_:)` (:818-821). Silent no-op when full; `removeFromModelList` (:823-825) is `modelList.removeAll { $0 == pin }` with no limit.
  ModelsSettingsPage.swift:64 - `Text("<pins.count> of <AppSettings.modelListLimit>. Click a model to set its reasoning effort and fast mode for every new chat.")`, 11pt, Chrome.secondaryText, `.padding(.horizontal, 4)`. IMPORTANT and unrecorded: this line is inside `if trimmed.isEmpty` (:63), so the count line only appears while the page's search field is empty.
  ModelsSettingsPage.swift:362 - `.help(isAdded ? "Remove from the picker" : (isFull ? "The picker holds up to <limit> models" : "Add to the picker"))`, where `isFull` is `settings.modelList.count >= AppSettings.modelListLimit` (:314). The add button is `.disabled(!isAdded && isFull)` (:361) and `.opacity(!isAdded && isFull ? 0.35 : 1)` (:364) with the comment that 0.35 is the page's disabled dimming. Accessibility label at :363: `isAdded ? "Remove <shortName> from the picker" : "Add <shortName> to the picker"`.
Rendered, the two user-visible strings are "<n> of 15. Click a model to set its reasoning effort and fast mode for every new chat." and "The picker holds up to 15 models".
resolutions.port_impact: Port the constant as 15, enforce it in the add path as a silent no-op, show the count line only when the search box is empty, and disable plus dim the add control to 0.35 opacity with tooltip "The picker holds up to 15 models" when full.

resolutions.finding: G8: R028 leaves HydraPanel.cornerRadius and HydraPanel.stripHeight unresolved although they set the whole panel geometry.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraPanel.swift:33 `static let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 22`; :37 `static let stripHeight: CGFloat = Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight + 6`. With Chrome.chromeTopPadding = 12 (Chrome.swift:32) and Chrome.capsuleHeight = capsuleContentHeight + capsuleVerticalPadding * 2 = 28 + 2*2 = 32 (Chrome.swift:33-34, :38), stripHeight = 12 + 32 + 6 = 50. HydraPanel.swift:40 also defines `static let finishHold: TimeInterval = 2.0`.
Derived numbers in UsageFloatingPanel: line 34 reports `onContentHeight($0 + HydraPanel.stripHeight + 8)` = measured + 58; line 35 `.padding(.top, HydraPanel.stripHeight)` = 50; line 36 `.padding(.bottom, 8)`; the empty branch reports `onContentHeight(HydraPanel.stripHeight + 44)` = 94 on appear (line 44) and pads top by 50 (line 42). The panel shape is `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: HydraPanel.cornerRadius, style: .continuous)` (line 25). The critic's arithmetic is exactly right.
Other verbatim geometry in the same file: scrim `(isDark ? Color.black : Color.white).opacity(isDark ? 0.3 : 0.34)` with `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(isDark ? 1 : 0.65), radius: 28, y: 10)` (lines 70-72); glass tint `Chrome.glassTint.opacity(isDark ? 0.22 : 0.16)` (line 61); title font `.system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium)` on `Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.92)` (lines 86-87); empty-state text `Text(verbatim: "Nothing to show for <provider.displayName> yet.")` at 13pt secondary (lines 39-41); close button `ChromeCircleButton(symbol: "xmark", help: "Dismiss the usage panel; the usage popover opens it again")` (line 105); the middle drag area carries `.help("Drag to move")` and the same accessibility label (lines 103-104).
resolutions.port_impact: Port with cornerRadius 22 and stripHeight 50 as derived constants (not magic numbers), so the terminal/team/usage panels stay in step, and report content height as measured + 58, or 94 for the empty state.

resolutions.finding: G9: R023 leaves AppSettings.defaultBackdropOpacity and the ChatZoom ladder unresolved although both drive reset affordances it documented.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. `static let defaultBackdropOpacity = 0.5` at AppSettings.swift:291; Key `backdropOpacity` = "backdropOpacity" at :135; property + didSet at :288-290; loaded at :713 as `defaults.object(forKey: Key.backdropOpacity) as? Double ?? Self.defaultBackdropOpacity`.
ChatZoom (DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift): line 10 `private static let percentages = [80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 125, 135]` - exactly 7 elements: 80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 125, 135. Line 11 `static var stepCount: Int { percentages.count }` = 7. Line 13 `static let defaultIndex = 3` (the 100% step). Lines 16-18 `clamped(_:) = min(stepCount - 1, max(0, index))`. Lines 20-22 `percentage(at:) = percentages[clamped(index)]`. Lines 25-27 `scale(at:) = CGFloat(percentage(at: index)) / 100`.
Where SettingsView uses them: :450-451 `ChatZoom.scale(at: index)` / `ChatZoom.percentage(at: index)`; :488 `private var isOffStock: Bool { index != ChatZoom.defaultIndex }`; :499 slider set `index = ChatZoom.clamped(Int($0.rounded()))`; :501 `in: 0...Double(ChatZoom.stepCount - 1)` i.e. 0...6; :514 reset `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.2)) { index = ChatZoom.defaultIndex }`; :531 `.accessibilityValue(Text("<percentage> percent"))`; and for the backdrop :540 `private var isOffStock: Bool { abs(value - AppSettings.defaultBackdropOpacity) >= 0.005 }`, :562 reset `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.2)) { value = AppSettings.defaultBackdropOpacity }`.
Also SOURCE FACT: ChatZoom.chatBaseSize maps text styles to points (ChatZoom.swift:45-57): largeTitle 26, title 22, title2 17, title3 15, headline and body 13, callout 12, subheadline 11, footnote/caption/caption2 10, @unknown default 13; and Font.chat returns the plain system style unmodified when zoom == 1 (:64-67), otherwise `Font.system(size: (chatBaseSize(style) * zoom).rounded(), ...)`, with headline defaulting to .semibold (:63).
resolutions.port_impact: Port: backdrop opacity default 0.5 under key "backdropOpacity", off-stock test abs(v - 0.5) >= 0.005; text-size slider 0...6 over the 7 percentages [80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 125, 135] with default index 3, off-stock test index != 3, both resets animated over 0.2 s. Keep the zoom==1 short-circuit so the default reads identically to an unzoomed layout.

resolutions.finding: G10: R023 omits the LicensesRow popover's three display titles and mis-describes the fallback string.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. SettingsView.swift:996-1000:
  `private static let files: [(title: String, resource: String)] = [ ("Droppy Code", "LICENSE"), ("Third-party notices", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES"), ("Trademarks", "TRADEMARK") ]`
Exactly 3 entries. NOTE the exact resource literals: "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES" and "TRADEMARK" carry NO ".md" in the literal; the extension is supplied separately at :1032 `withExtension: file.resource == "LICENSE" ? nil : "md"`. project.yml:29-34 ships LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md as resources of the app target.
  :1030-1035 `private static let texts: [String: String] = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: files.map { file in let url = Bundle.main.url(forResource: file.resource, withExtension: file.resource == "LICENSE" ? nil : "md"); let text = url.flatMap { try? String(contentsOf: $0, encoding: .utf8) } ?? "The <file.resource> file is missing from this copy of the app."; return (file.resource, text) })`
  :1037-1039 `private static func text(of resource: String) -> String { texts[resource] ?? "The <resource> file is missing from this copy of the app." }`
So the fallback interpolates the RESOURCE name, giving literally "The LICENSE file is missing from this copy of the app.", "The THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES file is missing from this copy of the app.", "The TRADEMARK file is missing from this copy of the app." - never the display title. Critic correct.
Popover shape: `.popover(isPresented: $isPresented, arrowEdge: .bottom)` containing a ScrollView of `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 18)` over `ForEach(Self.files, id: \.resource)`; per file a `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8)` with `Text(verbatim: file.title).font(.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold))` then `MarkdownView(text:).equatable().environment(\.markdownPointSize, 12).foregroundStyle(Chrome.secondaryText).textSelection(.enabled)`; `.padding(18)`, `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)`, outer `.frame(width: 480, height: 440).presentedChrome()`. The row itself: `ChromeRow(title: "Licenses", detail: "AGPL-3.0 with attribution terms, and the notices for what the app builds on.")` with `Button("Show")`. The comment at :1028-1029 explains the texts are read from the bundle once because the popover body re-runs on every hover and scroll.
resolutions.port_impact: Ship all three files with the app under the same base names, render each under its display title ("Droppy Code", "Third-party notices", "Trademarks") as Markdown at 12pt, read once at startup, and use the resource-name fallback sentence verbatim. Popover 480x440.

resolutions.finding: G11: TerminalPanel.swift:78 applies a persisted terminalHeight verbatim; the 140...760 clamp lives only in the drag handler.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. DroppyCode/App/Views/Terminal/TerminalPanel.swift:
  10 `@State private var dragOrigin: Double?`  13 `@State private var dragHeight: Double?`

resolutions.finding: G13: MCPSettingsPage's menu items set showMenu = false inconsistently; PopoverItem's dismissal contract is unrecorded.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT - the textual asymmetry is real, the behavioural consequence the critic infers is not.
The asymmetry, verbatim: MCPCustomRow menu (MCPSettingsPage.swift:555-568) - `PopoverItem("Edit", symbol: "pencil") { showMenu = false; isEditing = true }` (556-559), `PopoverItem("Disconnect", symbol: "xmark.circle", isEnabled: state.isConnected, isDestructive: true) { model.mcp.disconnect(entry) }` (560-562), `PopoverDivider()` (563), `PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true) { model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) }` (564-566). MCPConnectedRow menu (:180-194) - `PopoverItem("Refresh", symbol: "arrow.clockwise") { model.mcp.refresh(entry) }` (182-184), `PopoverItem("Show tools", symbol: "wrench") { showMenu = false; showTools = true }` (185-188), `PopoverDivider()` (189), `PopoverItem("Disconnect", ...) { model.mcp.disconnect(entry) }` (190-192).
PopoverItem's contract (UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift:253-273) settles it: the row's Button action is
  270 `guard !isConfirmed else { return }`
  271 `if let close = closePopoverBox?.close { close() } else { dismiss() }`
  273 `Task { @MainActor in action() }`  // comment: 'Runs after the popover closes, so an action that presents a sheet or alert is not swallowed.'
So EVERY PopoverItem dismisses its popover unconditionally BEFORE running the action, either through the injected `closePopoverBox` closure (Popovers.swift:180-185) or through `@Environment(\.dismiss)`. `showMenu = false` inside an action is therefore redundant - it runs a runloop turn after the binding has already been cleared. There is no behavioural difference between the items that set it and the ones that do not.
The `confirmation:` variant (Popovers.swift:255-268) is the only different path: it runs `action()` FIRST, flips to a checkmark with `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.22))`, then closes after `confirmationHold = .milliseconds(650)`; its doc comment says such an action 'must not present anything'. None of the MCP menu items use it.
Both MCP menus hang their popovers off the ellipsis button, not the row, with the comment 'On the button, not the row: hung from the row it opened in the row's middle' (MCPSettingsPage.swift:195, :568); the button is `Image(systemName: "ellipsis.circle").font(.system(size: 13)).foregroundStyle(Chrome.secondaryText).frame(width: 22, height: 22).contentShape(.rect)` with `.help("Server options")`.
resolutions.port_impact: Port PopoverItem-equivalents with one rule: close the menu first, then run the action asynchronously; and a confirmation variant that runs the action first, shows the confirmation label for 650 ms, then closes. The redundant close-the-menu writes in the MCP actions can be dropped without behaviour change, but keeping them is also harmless.

resolutions.finding: G14: Localized Text("...") vs Text(verbatim:) is inconsistent across the family; a port that treats them alike diverges wherever the catalog has an entry.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT - the textual inconsistency is real and the cited sites are right, but the stated consequence does not apply to this checkout.
Cited sites verified: UsagePanel.swift:36 `Text("Context window")` beside `Text(verbatim: "<tokens used> / <tokens window> (<percent>%)")` on :39; TerminalPanel.swift:68 `Text("No shell open in this thread")` and :71 `Button("New shell")`; MCPSetupPanel.swift:143 `Text("Checking")` beside `Text(verbatim: guide.reason)` (:123) and `Text(verbatim: step)` (:129). (The critic's line numbers 35/67/71/140 are each off by one to three.)
The disproof of the consequence: there is NO string catalog and NO localization in this checkout. `find` for "*.xcstrings", "*.strings", "*.lproj" and "*.stringsdict" across the whole tree returns nothing, and project.yml:5 sets `developmentLanguage: en` with the target's only resource-phase files being LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md (project.yml:29-34). With no catalog, a LocalizedStringKey resolves to its own key, so "Context window" renders as "Context window".
The one difference that IS live: LocalizedStringKey applies SwiftUI's inline Markdown parsing, Text(verbatim:) does not. None of the four cited strings contain Markdown-significant characters, so they render identically. The reason model- and data-derived strings use `verbatim:` is precisely that they may contain such characters, not localization.
resolutions.port_impact: The port needs no localization layer for parity. It DOES need to keep model- and data-derived strings out of any Markdown-rendering text path, which is the real distinction the source is drawing.

resolutions.finding: X1: Escape (raw keyCode 53) is handled in five places in this family, each with a different swallow policy, all via NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. Repo-wide, `keyCode == 53` appears at exactly 10 lines, counted: ChatBadge.swift:175, PromptEditor.swift:241, DiffInspector.swift:669, MCPKeyPanel.swift:66, MCPSetupPanel.swift:91, ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:600, TerminalPanel.swift:340, ThreadWindow.swift:49, AttachmentPreviewPanel.swift:204, LinkPopover.swift:56. Five of those are this family's, and their policies differ exactly as the critic says:
  1. DiffInspector.swift:668-671 - `guard event.keyCode == 53 else { return event }; close(); return nil`. Unconditional swallow while the monitor is installed (installed only between startMonitors/stopMonitors around a shown popover).
  2. TerminalPanel.swift:339-345 - `guard let view, event.keyCode == 53, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers).isEmpty, event.window?.firstResponder === view, TerminalSession.foregroundJobIsTheShell(view.process.shellPid) else { return event }; onEscapeAtPrompt(); return nil`. Four conjuncts; anything else passes Escape through to the terminal.
  3. MCPKeyPanel.swift:65-69 - `guard let self, self.panel?.isVisible == true, event.keyCode == 53 else { return event }; self.close(); return nil`.
  4. MCPSetupPanel.swift:90-94 - identical policy to (3).
  5. ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:598-602 - `if keyCode == 53, flags.isEmpty { cancel(); return }` inside handleKeyDown, where `flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers)`. So Escape WITH an allowed modifier held is judged as a chord candidate instead of cancelling. Its monitor (:545-554) matches [.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged] and returns nil for every one of those three types while `isActive`, i.e. it swallows all keyboard input during a recording; it also installs an NSApplication.didResignActiveNotification observer (:555-561) that calls cancel().
The critic's characterisation of (5) as 'cancels the recording' omits the `flags.isEmpty` condition.
resolutions.port_impact: Windows has no NSEvent local monitor. The port needs five separate decisions: a document-level capture keydown while the diff panel is open (swallow); a terminal keydown handler that only swallows Escape when the shell owns the foreground, no modifiers are held and the terminal has focus (see X7); two panel-level handlers that close while visible; and a recording mode that captures all key and modifier events, cancels on bare Escape only, and cancels on window blur.

SOURCE FACT. DiffInspector.swift:655-660, under the doc comment 'Clicks inside the panel pass through; any other click dismisses first but still reaches its target (e.g. another turn's Review button).':

TourWindowController.maxBottomPanelHeight (TourWindowController.swift:110-131): for each page builds `TourBottomPanelSizingView(page:buttonTitle: isLast ? finishButtonTitle : continueButtonTitle).frame(width: width)`, wraps it in `NSHostingView`, calls `hosting.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` and takes `hosting.fittingSize.height`, then `.max() ?? 0`. resolutions.finding: X7: The Terminal subsystem's hardest macOS dependency is TerminalStore's foregroundJobIsTheShell sysctl predicate, not SwiftTerm.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. DroppyCode/App/Views/Terminal/TerminalStore.swift:69-76 (the critic cites 69-77; the body ends at :76):
  69 `nonisolated static func foregroundJobIsTheShell(_ shell: pid_t) -> Bool {`
  70 `    guard shell > 0 else { return false }`
  71 `    var info = kinfo_proc()`
  72 `    var size = MemoryLayout<kinfo_proc>.stride`
  73 `    var name: [Int32] = [CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, shell]`
  74 `    guard sysctl(&name, 4, &info, &size, nil, 0) == 0, size > 0 else { return false }`
  75 `    return info.kp_eproc.e_tpgid == info.kp_eproc.e_pgid`
with the doc comment at :66-68: 'Whether the shell owns the foreground of its terminal: true at the prompt, false while a job it started (vim, claude, less) has the terminal. Read from the kernel's view of the shell, since the pty's master side answers no `tcgetpgrp` to a process it is not the controlling terminal of.'
Its only call site is TerminalPanel.swift:342, as the last conjunct of the Escape guard (X1 item 2). So the predicate gates exactly one behaviour: whether a bare Escape closes the terminal drawer or reaches the running program.
resolutions.port_impact: ConPTY has no process groups and no tpgid, so this cannot be translated. The port needs an explicit decision recorded as an ENGINEERING DECISION - e.g. track whether a child process other than the shell is running under the pty, or require a modifier or a different key to close the drawer - and must document that bare-Escape-at-prompt parity is approximated, not reproduced.

resolutions.finding: X8: The login-shell launch contract must be ported literally or replaced consciously.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. TerminalSession.init (TerminalStore.swift:17-41), in order:
  20 `view = LocalProcessTerminalView(frame: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 640, height: 240))`
  21 `view.font = NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular)`
  22 `view.optionAsMetaKey = true`
  28 `let shell = LoginEnvironment.userShell()`
  29-33 `var environment = LoginEnvironment.current` then exactly four overrides: `environment["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"`, `environment["COLORTERM"] = "truecolor"`, `environment["TERM_PROGRAM"] = "Droppy Code"`, `environment["DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT"] = directory`
  34 `let pairs = environment.map { "<key>=<value>" }`
  35 `let shellName = "-" + (shell as NSString).lastPathComponent`
  36-39 `var arguments: [String] = []; if let command { arguments = ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"] }`
  40 `view.startProcess(executable: shell, args: arguments, environment: pairs, execName: shellName, currentDirectory: directory)`
Supporting facts the critic did not pin: `LoginEnvironment.userShell()` (Core/Support/Shell.swift:425-435) returns `$SHELL` if it is an executable file, else the passwd entry's pw_shell if executable, else the literal "/bin/zsh". `LoginEnvironment.current` (:337-339) is the cached login-shell environment or `fallbackEnvironment`; it is produced by `read()` (:363-388) running `Shell.run(shell, ["-l", "-i", "-c", "printf '__DROPPY_CODE_ENVIRONMENT__'; /usr/bin/env -0; printf '__DROPPY_CODE_ENVIRONMENT__'"], timeout: 8)` and parsing NUL-separated entries between the two markers, dropping an excludedKeys set of exactly 15 names (:331-336): "_", "SHLVL", "PWD", "OLDPWD", "TERM", "TERM_PROGRAM", "TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION", "TERM_SESSION_ID", "COLORTERM", "ITERM_SESSION_ID", "XPC_SERVICE_NAME", "__CFBundleIdentifier", "CLAUDECODE", "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT", "CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT"; then `environment["PATH"] = augmentedPath(environment["PATH"])`, which appends any missing entries of a 12-element literal list, in order (:439-444): "/opt/homebrew/bin", "/opt/homebrew/sbin", "/usr/local/bin", "<home>/.local/bin", "<home>/.bun/bin", "<home>/.cargo/bin", "<home>/.npm-global/bin", "<home>/.volta/bin", "/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin".
Note the excluded TERM/COLORTERM/TERM_PROGRAM are exactly three of the four keys TerminalSession then sets back explicitly.
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows terminal cannot use `-` argv[0] login semantics. Port this as an explicit replacement: choose the user's shell, start it in the project directory, and set the same four environment variables (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, TERM_PROGRAM=<app name>, <APP>_PROJECT_ROOT=<directory>). The script-tab form must run the command and then hand the session back to an interactive shell, matching `"<command>; exec <shell> -l"`. Record the PATH augmentation list as a Windows-specific decision, not a translation.

resolutions.finding: X9: Persisted state in this family is AppSettings/UserDefaults with literal keys plus the Keychain and mcp.json; the update checker adds three keys nobody names.
resolutions.truth:
SOURCE FACT. The family's own AppSettings keys, verbatim from AppSettings.swift's Key enum: "confirmBeforeDeleting" (:123, default true at :702), "backdropOpacity" (:135, default 0.5 at :713), "terminalHeight" (:144, default 260 at :722), "modelList" (:145), "modelPreferences" (:146), "hasSeenTour" (:177, default false at :745). AppSettings writes through `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard` (:183), so a capture run redirects them to the suite "iordv.droppycode.website-captures" (CaptureRun.swift:44).
Non-UserDefaults stores: (a) MCP secrets in the Keychain via MCPKeychain (account derived from server+field, MCPKeychain.swift:7-9), written by `model.mcp.saveCustomValues` (MCPStore.swift:215) and deleted by `MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server:)` from MCPStore.disconnect (MCPStore.swift:124); MCPKeychain.value returns nil outright in a capture run (`guard !CaptureRun.isEnabled else { return nil }`, MCPKeychain.swift:12). (b) Non-secret custom-server variable values in mcp.json, as the lock toggle's own help string states verbatim at MCPSettingsPage.swift:791: `.help(variable.isSecret ? "Kept in the Keychain" : "Stored in mcp.json; click to keep it in the Keychain instead")`.
(c) UpdateChecker's three keys, on UserDefaults.standard and NOT on the captures suite: "updateChecker_release", "updateChecker_lastChecked", "updateChecker_notifiedVersion" (UpdateChecker.swift:77-81). See G12.
resolutions.port_impact: Map each key one-for-one in the port's settings store with the same names and defaults, keep MCP secrets in Windows DPAPI-protected storage and non-secret values in the project's mcp.json, and keep the update-checker keys in a separate store that a test or capture profile does not redirect (or consciously decide to redirect them and record the divergence).

upstream_defects: DiffInspector.swift:627-636 and :640-657 - DiffPopoverCoordinator.show() increments `session` (line 629) without assigning `pendingSession`, while `pendingSession` is only re-synchronized in close() (:576-577) and reopen()'s anchor-changed branch (:607-608). Consequence: any popover close the coordinator did not itself initiate (NSPopover.behavior = .semitransient at :536 closing on its own, or the anchor view leaving its window) reaches popoverDidClose with session != pendingSession, so the guard at :649 is false and the close neither clears `shownRuntime.isDiffVisible` (:650) nor drops `popover.contentViewController` (:653). The thread stays flagged as showing its diff and the inspector view tree stays alive observing the runtime. Reachable from the very first show(), since session becomes 1 while pendingSession is still 0. Reproduce, do not fix.

MCPSettingsPage.swift:564-566 - the custom-server ellipsis menu's Delete runs `model.mcp.deleteCustom(server)` on one click with no confirmation, ignoring `settings.confirmBeforeDeleting` (default true, AppSettings.swift:702) which every other destructive path in Settings and the sidebar honours (SettingsView.swift:851, :892; SidebarView.swift:192, :360, :891). deleteCustom also runs disconnect(), which deletes the server's Keychain secrets (MCPStore.swift:124, :193-199). Reproduce, do not fix.

MCPKeyPanel.swift:15-31 - present() has no `isPresenting` re-entry guard (unlike MCPSetupPanel.swift:18-26) and close() (:33-36) clears no presented-entry id. A second present for the same entry re-opens `entry.keysURL` in the user's browser (:16-18), re-measures, rebuilds the hosting controller and re-positions the panel, discarding anything typed into the fields. Reachable from MCPSettingsPage.swift:356, :538 and :973. Reproduce, do not fix.

TerminalPanel.swift:80 and AppSettings.swift:722 - `.frame(height: dragHeight ?? model.settings.terminalHeight)` applies the persisted terminal height with no clamp, and the load path is `defaults.object(forKey:) as? Double ?? 260` with no clamp either; the 140...760 clamp exists only inside the drag's onChange (:89). A stored value outside that range (older build, hand-edited plist) is applied verbatim and can only be corrected by dragging. Contrast ChatZoom.clamped (ChatZoom.swift:16-18), which does clamp a stored index on read. Reproduce, do not fix.

UsageFloatingPanel.swift:82-84 vs UsagePanel.swift:29 - the floating panel's title capsule draws a second ProviderIcon whenever `headsProvider != nil`, while the panel body suppresses the heads section unless `headsProvider != provider`. A Hydra pair whose heads run on the lead's own provider therefore shows the same provider icon twice in the strip. Reproduce, do not fix.

UsagePanel.swift:32 - `showsContext = usage?.fraction != nil && usage?.windowTokens != nil` is a redundant conjunction: ContextUsage.fraction (Timeline.swift:301-304) already returns nil unless windowTokens is non-nil and > 0. Harmless dead condition; copy it or simplify it, but do not treat the two operands as independent.

MCPSettingsPage.swift:182-192 and :556-566 - four of the six PopoverItem actions omit `showMenu = false` while two set it. Since PopoverItem always closes its popover before running the action (Popovers.swift:270-273), the writes are redundant in both directions. Dead defensive code, not a behaviour difference.

SettingsView.swift:926-929 - AboutSoftwareUpdateSection is the first child of the About page's `VStack(spacing: Chrome.sectionSpacing)` but renders nothing unless `checker.updateAvailable` (AboutUpdateViews.swift:731-733). On the common path it is a zero-height container that the parent VStack still separates from the app card by section spacing, so the About page carries an extra gap above the app card whenever no update is waiting.
dead_or_unreachable: DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift (whole file, including the TourWindowController.present call at :216-220) and DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift are shipped, non-#if-guarded code reachable ONLY when the binary is launched with `--website-captures <folder>` or `--tour-captures <folder>`. Proof: CaptureRun.outputDirectory (Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift:10-19) scans CommandLine.arguments for exactly those two flags and requires a following argument; isEnabled = outputDirectory != nil (:32); isTourRun requires `--tour-captures` plus a following argument (:21-25); AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching branches on WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled and returns early (:11-14); WebsiteCaptures.run dispatches to TourCaptures.run at WebsiteCaptures.swift:304. The invocation is documented in TourCaptures.swift:7 as `open -n -W "Droppy Code.app" --args --tour-captures <folder>`. Not dead, but never reached by a user launch.

UpdateChecker.previewVersion (UpdateChecker.swift:101, assigned at :121-124) is reachable only via the launch argument `--preview-update <version>`; the comment at :119-121 documents it as a way to show the update story without a newer release. Tool-only path.

The capture-mode short circuits are user-unreachable for the same reason and must not be ported as runtime behaviour: MCPKeychain.value returns nil when CaptureRun.isEnabled (MCPKeychain.swift:12); APIKeychain returns "" (APIKeychain.swift:14); ProviderRegistry.swift:162, :176, :210, :538, :669, :703 all branch on it; Storage.swift:20 redirects the store root; Library.swift:200 and ProviderRegistry.swift:161, :698 use CaptureRun.defaults; AppSettings uses `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard` (AppSettings.swift:183); DiffPopoverCoordinator.sync keeps `runtime.isDiffVisible` set on adoption only when WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled (DiffInspector.swift:557, :563).

Localization is inert in this checkout: `Text("...")` / `Button("...")` LocalizedStringKey lookups can never resolve to anything but their own key, because no .xcstrings, .strings, .stringsdict or .lproj exists anywhere in the tree and project.yml:5 declares only `developmentLanguage: en`. The only live effect of the localized form is SwiftUI's inline Markdown parsing.

PopoverItem's `confirmation:` branch (Popovers.swift:255-268, confirmationHold .milliseconds(650)) is never exercised by any menu item in this family: none of the six MCP menu items nor the archive delete items pass `confirmation:`. Live elsewhere in the app, unreachable through this family's surfaces.

MCPKeyPanel.stopEscapeMonitor (MCPKeyPanel.swift:72-75) and MCPSetupPanel.stopEscapeMonitor (:97-100) run only from close(). Neither panel installs a window-close or resign-key observer, so a panel hidden by any other route would leave its application-wide keyDown monitor installed. In this checkout no such route exists: both panels' traffic lights are hidden (:56-58 and :81-83) and their content's only dismissal is the onDone closure that calls close(), so the leak is not reachable. Recorded because removing the traffic-light hiding in a port would make it reachable.
still_unresolved: Whether NSPopover.behavior = .semitransient ever closes the diff popover WITHOUT the coordinator's own [.leftMouseDown, .rightMouseDown] local monitor having run close() first is not decidable from this source alone: it depends on AppKit's semitransient dismissal triggers (app deactivation, the anchor window resigning key, the anchor view being removed), which are not in the checkout. The structural fact (session != pendingSession after any show()) is proven from source; the frequency of the resulting leak is not. Needed evidence: AppKit runtime behaviour, or an instrumented run of the real app.

Whether the empty AboutSoftwareUpdateSection VStack contributes one or two instances of Chrome.sectionSpacing (20) to the About page's layout is a SwiftUI layout-engine question, not a source question. The source fact is that it is an always-present child that renders no content unless an update is waiting. Needed evidence: a measured screenshot of the About page with and without a waiting update.
